WHAT’S HAPPENING

Somewhere in the last few years, you disappeared.

You still go to work. You still show up. But the gut came in and never left, your face is puffy every morning, and you’re asleep in the chair with the TV on before dinner’s even on the table. The stairs wind you. And at home, things have gone quiet. She’s noticed. So have you.

WHAT’S REALLY GOING ON

It isn’t your age. It’s your arteries.

Every part of you runs on what your blood delivers: your heart, your muscles, your brain, your drive. About 100,000 heartbeats a day push it through some 60,000 miles of blood vessels.

As artery walls stiffen and narrow over the years, a little less gets through every year. Nothing breaks all at once. Your energy, your body and your edge just fade together, slowly enough that you blame it on getting older.

Out of breath on the stairs?

3

Mistake: Thinking all garlic is the same

Raw garlic, garlic powder, garlic oil and aged garlic are not the same thing. Aging changes garlic’s chemistry: the harsh compounds in raw garlic turn into gentler, more stable ones like S-allyl cysteine, the marker of aged garlic quality.

Instead: Look for aged garlic, and check the marker. Resilia’s pouch says it plainly: standardized for S-allyl cysteine.†
